event.canonical_title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Tankers Raise Oil Price Concerns
event.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels, backed by Iran, have attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, raising concerns about the future of oil and gas prices. This incident may represent a new front in the ongoing conflict involving the US and Iran, prompting discussions on its potential economic impact, particularly on gas prices in the United States.

event_overview.title: About Middle East Conflict
event_overview.subject: Middle East Conflict
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the risk that attacks by Yemen’s Houthi movement (Ansar Allah) on Saudi-linked oil shipping or energy infrastructure could widen the Yemen and Red Sea security crisis and disrupt oil flows. It sits within the longer Yemen conflict, in which Houthi forces took Sana’a in 2014 and Saudi Arabia led a military coalition from 2015, alongside a separate pattern of Houthi attacks on commercial navigation in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

facts.label: Origins of the Yemen conflict
facts.value: Houthi forces captured Yemen’s capital, Sana’a, in September 2014; the UN Security Council records that they then sought in January 2015 to replace the government with a Houthi-dominated authority.

facts.label: Saudi Arabia’s role
facts.value: Saudi Arabia formed and led a coalition that began military operations in Yemen in March 2015 after Yemen’s president requested external support; the conflict subsequently included Houthi cross-border missile, drone and rocket attacks on Saudi territory.

facts.label: Relevant waterways
facts.value: The maritime dimension centers on the Red Sea, the Bab al-Mandab strait and the Gulf of Aden—routes used by merchant vessels moving between the Suez Canal and the Indian Ocean.

facts.label: International legal and diplomatic frame
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2216 (2015) demanded that the Houthis end violence, withdraw from seized areas and refrain from threats or provocations against neighboring states; Resolution 2722 (2024) demanded an immediate end to Houthi attacks on merchant and commercial vessels in the Red Sea.

facts.label: Ceasefire context
facts.value: A UN-brokered Yemen truce began on April 2, 2022 and formally expired on October 2, 2022. The UN says the overall front-line military situation remained comparatively stable afterward, while its Special Envoy continued pursuing a nationwide ceasefire and Yemeni-led political settlement.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the July 2026 escalation involving alleged Houthi attacks, oil-price concerns and related U.S.-Iran diplomacy; it does not attempt to chronicle the full Yemen war, every Red Sea incident, or all regional negotiations.
